Extreme learning machine model for state.novelty: This paper introduces an improved state of charge (SOC) estimation model for lithium-ion batteries that combines Extreme Learning Machine (ELM) with Gravitational Search Algorithm (GSA) to optimize the number of hidden layer neurons, enhancing accuracy without requiring internal battery knowledge.
Extreme learning machine model for state.key_result: The ELM-GSA model demonstrates high accuracy and a lower SOC error rate compared to BPNN-GSA and RBFNN-GSA models.

Online jointprediction of multi-forward-.novelty: This paper introduces a novel machine-learning-enabled method for real-time multi-forward-step state of charge (SOC) prediction using LSTM neural networks combined with multiple linear regression, addressing the inefficiencies of existing model-based techniques under complex real-world conditions.
Online jointprediction of multi-forward-.key_result: The LSTM-based model demonstrates fast and accurate multi-forward-step prediction for battery SOC, achieving a root mean square error (RMSE) as small as 2%.

Real-time state of charge estimation of.novelty: This paper introduces an optimized Random Forest Regression (RFR) algorithm using a Differential Search Algorithm (DSA) to enhance state of charge estimation of lithium-ion batteries without requiring detailed battery chemistry knowledge.
Real-time state of charge estimation of.key_result: The DSA optimized RFR algorithm achieves an RMSE of 0.382% in the HPPC test and an MAE of 0.193% and 0.346% in DST and FUDS cycles, respectively, at 25°C.

SOC estimation of Li-ion battery using c.novelty: This paper introduces a SOC estimation method using a U-Net architecture that can handle variable-length input data and accurately estimate SOC values at the starting point, addressing limitations of traditional data-driven methods.
SOC estimation of Li-ion battery using c.key_result: The proposed method achieves a mean absolute error (MAE) within 1.1% and a root-mean-square error (RMSE) within 1.4% at constant temperatures.

State of charge estimation for lithium-i.novelty: The paper introduces an improved barnacle mating optimizer (IBMO) that enhances the performance of the support vector machine (SVM) for state of charge (SOC) estimation in lithium-ion batteries, achieving high accuracy and reliability.
State of charge estimation for lithium-i.key_result: The proposed model achieves a root mean squared error (RMSE) of 0.0042, a mean absolute percentage error (MAPE) of 0.61%, and an R-square (R2) of 0.9994, outperforming four comparison models.

State of charge estimation of lithium-io.novelty: This paper introduces a method for estimating the state of charge (SOC) of lithium-ion batteries using a Temporal Convolutional Network (TCN) that can adapt to different battery types through transfer learning with minimal data.
State of charge estimation of lithium-io.key_result: The proposed method achieves an average MAE of 0.67% for SOC estimation across various ambient temperature conditions.

State-of-charge estimation of lithium-io.novelty: This paper introduces a method that combines long short-term memory (LSTM) networks with an unscented Kalman filter (UKF) to improve state-of-charge (SOC) estimation of lithium-ion batteries under varying temperatures, addressing limitations of traditional methods.
State-of-charge estimation of lithium-io.key_result: The proposed method achieves root mean square errors less than 1.1% and mean average errors less than 1% in SOC estimation.

State_of_Charge_Estimation_of_Lithium-Io.novelty: This paper presents a novel hybrid model that combines NARX neural networks with LSTM to address the issues of gradient explosion and vanishing gradients, improving the accuracy of state of charge estimation for lithium-ion batteries.
State_of_Charge_Estimation_of_Lithium-Io.key_result: The proposed hybrid NARX-LSTM model achieves an RMSE of less than 1%, which is approximately 60% better than the standard LSTM.

Support Vector Machines Used to Estimate.novelty: This paper presents a support vector machine (SVM) approach for estimating the state of charge (SOC) of lithium iron manganese phosphate batteries, claiming improved accuracy over traditional methods such as current integration and Kalman filters.
Support Vector Machines Used to Estimate.key_result: The SVM SOC estimator maintains a high level of accuracy, better than 6% over all ranges of operation.

Uncorrelated sparse autoencoder with lon.novelty: The paper introduces the Uncorrelated Sparse Autoencoder with Long Short-Term Memory (USAL), which combines sparse autoencoders and LSTM networks to improve long-term state-of-charge estimations in lithium-ion batteries by penalizing high correlations between encodings.
Uncorrelated sparse autoencoder with lon.key_result: USAL outperforms benchmarked models when trained on five initial charge-discharge cycles across multiple battery cells using three publicly available accelerated aging datasets.
